class.name: VegetationMist3D
class.brief_description: Ground mist in the near field, simulated with NVIDIA Flow.
class.description: Radiation fog lying over the ground around the camera (or [member follow_target]), as a real gas in a [code]PhysXFlow3D[/code] of its own: it parts round bodies that walk through it, drifts with the ground wind and drains into hollows, since it is heavier than the air above it. A round patch of [member mist_range] is cut into cells of [member mist_cell]; each cell holds a flat box emitter on the ground that keeps the layer at its level and refills what a walker stirs away. Cells in hollows (lower than a ring 10 m round them) get more mist and cells on crests less, as cooled air pools in hollows. With [member mist_amount] below [code]0[/code], the level comes from [member weather_map]: radiation fog needs air near saturation (humidity over about 0.88), calm air (under about 3 m/s at 10 m), a clear sky, and no sun to burn it off, so it fades as [member sun_light] climbs from 4 to 18 degrees. Beyond the patch, wide haze belongs to the environment's fog. Flow is drawn by its own ray marcher and is not path traced yet. Needs an engine built with [code]flow_sdk=[/code] and the Flow libraries beside it; without them this node shows a warning and does nothing.

method.name: get_active_cells
method.description: How many cells held mist last step.

method.name: get_mist_level
method.description: The mist level in use: [member mist_amount], or the weather's level when that is below [code]0[/code].

method.name: get_propensity_at
method.description: How much mist the cell at [param position] gathers relative to level ground: above [code]1[/code] in hollows, below it on crests (0.15 to 2).

method.name: weather_mist_level
method.description: The mist level the weather and the sun give now (0 to 1), whatever [member mist_amount] is.

members.member: Off: the cells stop feeding the gas and the mist evaporates.

Extinction per metre at level [code]1[/code]. Thin ground fog is 0.01 to 0.05 per metre, thick valley fog up to 0.2 (Kunkel 1984): hardly visible across a metre, closing the view along the ground over tens of metres.
The gas's cell size in metres.
Centre of the mist patch. Empty: the viewport's camera.
How much heavier than the air the mist is: the flow's [code]smoke_buoyancy[/code] is minus this. Air a few degrees colder is 1 to 2 % denser, so the mist slides down slopes and pools.
The mist level, 0 to 2. Below [code]0[/code]: from the weather (see [method weather_mist_level]).
Size of a mist cell (one emitter) in metres.
Colour of the mist, lit by the sun. Its droplets scatter strongly forward, so it glows looking towards a low sun.
Depth of the layer the cells hold, in metres; shallow ground fog is under 2 m.
Radius of the mist patch in metres. Its GPU memory grows with its area.
The [DirectionalLight3D] whose height burns the mist off. Empty: the sun does not count.
The terrain the cells stand on and the gas lies on: any node with [code]get_height(position)[/code] (TerrainGenerator3D, Terrain3D). Empty: a ray down onto static bodies.
The [WeatherMap3D] for the mist level and the ground wind.
